source.test: VanillaDownloader.listVersions() JSONSerialization guard vs a JSON-syntax parse failure

cases.name: valid-json-wrong-shape
cases.note: syntactically valid JSON, but not the expected top-level object with a "versions" array

cases.name: syntactically-invalid-json
cases.note: fails to parse as JSON at all

cases.name: valid-json-wrong-shape
cases.mechanism: the `guard let root = try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(...) as? [String: Any] ... else { throw ... }` cast fails (line 381-384), and the custom error fires

cases.name: syntactically-invalid-json
cases.error: not ServerJarProviderError at all -- an uncaught Foundation JSON parse error
cases.mechanism: `try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data)` (line 381) is a plain `try`, not `try?` -- when the bytes are not valid JSON syntax, JSONSerialization itself throws before the guard's `as?` cast ever runs, so the custom invalidResponse wrapping never applies

notes: A real distinction every one of the six providers shares, worth preserving precisely in the Rust port: "valid JSON with the wrong shape" and "not valid JSON at all" are NOT the same failure path in MSC 1. The former is caught by the guard's failed type-cast and produces a friendly, provider-specific `invalidResponse(String)` message. The latter propagates as whatever raw error `JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with:)` throws (a Foundation `NSError`/Cocoa error, not one of `ServerJarProviderError`'s three cases) straight out of the function, since none of these call sites wrap the parse call in `try?` or a `do`/`catch`. A Rust `serde_json::from_slice` parse error and a custom "malformed shape" domain error are the natural two-variant mapping -- collapsing them into one error type would lose a distinction MSC 1 itself has (even if only as an accident of `try` vs `try?`, not a designed one).
